At 300 bit/s, BFSK and DBPSK symbols las: At 300 bit/s, BFSK and DBPSK symbols last about 3.33 milliseconds; DQPSK symbols last about 6.67 milliseconds and carry two bits each. At 100 bit/s, symbols last three times as long. A slower transfer takes longer but can be easier to decode. File sizes matter: 8 KiB takes several minutes even before repeated copies.
At the same bit rate, DQPSK uses half as: At the same bit rate, DQPSK uses half as many symbols per second as BFSK or DBPSK; it is not twice as fast at a fixed bit rate. Its four phase choices are closer together, so noise and echoes can make them harder to distinguish. Phase modes are experimental: start with a short message and a quiet room.
